about: Registry of design-criteria guardrails. A rule is ACTIVE only if its text was read from a public source or its numbers are supplied by the user from a licensed copy with the clause and edition named. Nothing is filled in from memory. Guardrails report; they never change a simulation result or a published number. Tier 'advisory' rules come from trade articles and forum discussions, not standards: they never produce a violation, only an advisory, and each lists how its sources were read (read, snippet-only, or blocked by a bot challenge, which is never bypassed). Disagreement between sources is recorded with the rule.

rules.clause: (d)(2)(i)(D) safe upper and lower limits for items such as temperatures, pressures, flows or compositions
rules.how: the case declares safe limits per stream in design_limits.streams (T_C, P_kPa, mass_kg_h, with an anchor); every simulated stream is checked against them in every scenario and package. The regulation sets no numbers: the limits are the process's own.

rules.clause: (d)(2)(i)(E) evaluation of the consequences of deviations; (f)(1)(ii) operating limits: consequences of deviation
rules.how: a case that simulates scenarios (deviations) but declares no safe limits is reported as a coverage gap, because the deviations then have no consequence criterion.

rules.clause: (d)(3)(i)(G) material and energy balances for processes built after May 26, 1992
rules.tolerance_source: tool default, not from the regulation (it sets no number)
rules.how: feed mass equals product mass in the simulated flowsheet.

rules.clause: (a)(19)(i) to (v) categories 1 to 4 by flashpoint and boiling point; liquids heated for use to within 30 F (16.7 C) of their flashpoint are handled as the next more hazardous category
rules.how: needs flashpoint and boiling point per compound in design_limits.compounds (from a safety data sheet, with an anchor); applies to streams that are at least 99.9 % mass one such compound, since a mixture's flashpoint is not available. Reports the category and whether the simulated temperature triggers the heated-near-flashpoint rule: an information status, not a violation.

rules.standard: API Standard 520 / 521 (pressure-relieving systems), ASME BPVC overpressure
rules.clause: allowable accumulation over the set pressure
rules.source: not read: the standards are sold or behind a free-read-only login, which this tool does not bypass
rules.how: ACTIVE ONLY WHEN the case supplies design_limits.relief.<unit> = {set_pressure_kPa, accumulation_pct, anchor naming the clause and edition} from a licensed copy; the stream pressure at that unit is then checked against set pressure x (1 + accumulation/100). No accumulation value is built in.

rules.source: not read: free-access view requires a login, which this tool does not use
rules.how: registered so the gap is visible; no check is implemented until the user supplies clauses and numbers from a licensed copy.

rules.clause: design pressure at least the maximum operating pressure plus the greater of 10 % or 25 psi (172.4 kPa)

sources.how_read: blocked by a bot challenge; known only from a search-result summary
sources.says: about 10 % or 25 psi above maximum operating pressure, whichever is greater; the 10 % suits higher pressures, 25 psi lower

sources.how_read: search-result summary only (a file download, not fetched)
sources.says: the same greater-of rule in a university process-design document

sources.how_read: blocked by a bot challenge; search-result summary only
sources.says: the margin is owner preference, not set by ASME VIII; 10 % is typical

rules.disagreement: a '1.1 x or 30 psi' variant appears in a forum question with no reference found; the 10 %-or-25-psi form is the one repeated across sources
rules.how: needs design_limits.vessels.<unit>: operating stream, design pressure with its basis (gauge or absolute) and an anchor; the rule is applied to gauge pressure (the sources do not say; this is my assumption). Advisory if the design pressure is below the rule.

rules.clause: design temperature above maximum operating temperature by about 15 to 20 C (SPE) or 28 C / 50 F (forum replies and a university process-design document)

sources.says: usually 15 to 20 C above the maximum continuous operating temperature

sources.how_read: blocked by a bot challenge; search-result summary only
sources.says: 50 F below design temperature recommended in some practices; the margin is the owner's judgement

rules.disagreement: 15 to 20 C, 28 C and 50 F are all quoted; pipelines and exchangers cited with 10 C and 30 C
rules.how: needs design_limits.vessels.<unit>.design_temperature_C and an operating stream: pass at or above +27.8 C, advisory between +15 and +27.8 C (inside the quoted range), advisory below +15 C.

rules.clause: NPSH available below NPSH required means the pump loses more than the 3 % head used to define NPSHR

sources.says: published NPSHR is usually based on a 3 % head drop

rules.how: needs design_limits.pumps.<unit>: suction stream, NPSHR (m, from the pump data sheet), liquid vapour pressure (kPa) and density (kg/m3) with anchors; NPSHA = (suction pressure - vapour pressure) / (density x g) + static head, friction ignored. A ratio below 1.0 is a violation by definition.

rules.clause: NPSH margin ratio NPSHA/NPSHR: typically 1.0 to 1.3 minimum for low suction energy; 1.1 to 1.5 with mitigating factors; 1.5 to 2.0 for cold or warm water; 2.0 to 2.5 for very high suction energy

sources.how_read: read in full from a Wayback copy (the live page gave a bot challenge, which was not bypassed)
sources.says: the ranges above; reliability trends up to a ratio near 4.0

rules.disagreement: another trade source gives 1.2 to 1.6 to cover the 3 % head drop, and a vendor page a fixed 1 m margin (not verified); the Hydraulic Institute range is wider
rules.how: the pump entry declares suction_energy: low, mitigated, cold_warm_water or very_high; ratio below the lower end is an advisory, inside the range is information, above it passes.

rules.clause: control valve pressure drop at least 20 % of the total system pressure drop or 10 psi (0.7 bar), whichever is greater

sources.how_read: the opening of the article read; the rest is behind a login
sources.says: 20 % of total system pressure drop or 10 psi if the engineer can dictate it; valves are most responsive 60 to 80 % open; rules of thumb are for preliminary selection only

sources.how_read: page text is script-rendered and came back empty; search-result summary only
sources.says: 33 % of dynamic losses or 15 psi for pumped circuits; other bases for compressors and steam

rules.disagreement: 20 %, 30 %, 33 % and 50 % of the friction drop are all quoted, on different bases (total system or friction only)
rules.how: needs design_limits.valves.<unit>: inlet stream, outlet stream and the total system pressure drop with an anchor; the valve drop comes from the simulation. Advisory below the 20 % / 0.7 bar rule, information between it and 33 %.

rules.clause: a liquid that flashes across a valve (downstream pressure at or below vapour pressure) needs a full flashing and cavitation calculation, not a rule of thumb

sources.says: flashing leaves a liquid-gas mixture downstream; cavitation can occur below the choked pressure drop

rules.how: for any valve with inlet and outlet streams declared in design_limits.valves, an outlet vapour fraction above the inlet's by more than 0.001 is reported as information.
